cim: Aramco acquires 49% stake in Humain in $2.6bn AI deal - middle-east-online.com
cim_eredeti: Aramco acquires 49% stake in Humain in $2.6bn AI deal - middle-east-online.com
szoveg_eredeti:
RIYADH – Saudi Aramco has completed the acquisition of a 49% stake in artificial intelligence company Humain, in a deal involving approximately SAR 9.9 billion ($2.6 billion) in cash contributions during 2026, alongside the transfer of key AI, computing and digital assets.

The transaction, announced on Sunday by Aramco and Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), leaves the sovereign wealth fund with a 51% controlling stake in Humain. Aramco acquired its share through a wholly owned subsidiary.

The partnership is designed to accelerate Humain’s expansion and strengthen its position in the global artificial intelligence market by combining the two shareholders’ technology investments, expertise and capabilities.

Under the agreement, Aramco and PIF will oversee Humain’s expansion plans and support the development of an integrated AI ecosystem covering data centres, high-performance computing infrastructure, advanced models, applications and specialised industry solutions.

Humain is targeting the deployment of 3 gigawatts of AI data centre capacity by 2030, as it seeks to meet growing demand for computing power across regional and international markets.

The company is also developing cloud platforms and advanced AI models, including ALLaM, a multimodal large language model designed to support Arabic-language applications.

For Aramco, the investment provides an opportunity to extend the use of artificial intelligence across its industrial operations and strengthen the commercial value of its existing digital technologies. The company expects Humain’s infrastructure and services to support operational performance and create additional opportunities for revenue growth.

Aramco President and CEO Amin Nasser said the partnership would reinforce the company’s position as a global technology leader and support the development of Saudi Arabia’s domestic AI industry.

He added that Aramco had generated $11.3 billion in technology realised value since 2023, with a significant portion attributed to AI solutions.

PIF Deputy Governor and Head of MENA Investments Yazeed Al-Humied said bringing the two organisations’ AI investment portfolios together under Humain would strengthen technological development, talent growth and intellectual property creation.

The transaction builds on an agreement between Aramco and PIF in October 2025, when the two organisations outlined plans to combine selected AI assets and capabilities under Humain, with PIF retaining majority ownership.

Launched in May 2025, Humain is developing capabilities across four main areas: next-generation data centres, high-performance computing infrastructure and cloud platforms, advanced AI models, and specialised AI applications and solutions.

The completed transaction marks a significant step in Saudi Arabia’s efforts to expand its artificial intelligence infrastructure and establish a stronger presence in the global technology market.
